content: Before taking any medication, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, maintain a comprehensive list of all substances you use and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist to avoid potential interactions or complications. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the symptoms are less severe, contact a poison control center without delay. For U.S. residents, the poison control hotline is 1-800-222-1222. To prevent the transmission of hepatitis B to others, always practice safer sex by using effective barrier methods such as latex condoms or dental dams during sexual activity. Do not share needles under any circumstances. While taking this medication, your doctor may recommend laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney and liver function tests or HIV tests, to monitor your health. It is crucial to attend all scheduled medical appointments during and for several months after completing treatment. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your health needs. Warning: Discontinuing treatment with adefovir dipivoxil can lead to severe worsening of hepatitis, which in rare cases may result in death. If your doctor instructs you to stop taking this medication, they will closely monitor you for signs of worsening hepatitis. Rarely, severe and potentially fatal liver and blood acid-base balance problems (lactic acidosis) have been reported in patients, particularly those who are overweight, using similar medications (nucleoside analogs such as didanosine or stavudine). Additionally, adefovir dipivoxil may cause kidney problems, especially in patients with pre-existing kidney disease. If you have untreated HIV infection, taking adefovir dipivoxil may lead to the development of HIV resistance, rendering standard HIV medications ineffective. An HIV test is recommended before and during treatment to ensure appropriate therapy. This medication is used to treat chronic hepatitis B, a viral infection of the liver. It works by slowing the growth of the virus, thereby reducing the amount of virus in the body. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. Use it consistently to achieve the best results. To help you remember, take it at the same time each day. Do not increase, decrease, or stop the dosage without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. Treatment with adefovir alone is not suitable for patients co-infected with hepatitis B and HIV. Worsening of your condition, reduced response to treatment, or infection with resistant strains of the virus may occur during or after treatment. Common side effects may include weakness, headache, fever, increased cough, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or gas. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before starting adefovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. For any concerns or side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the U.S., you can also report side effects to the FDA. In Canada, consult your healthcare provider for guidance.
